Hi Product Hunt, I'm Andrew, the maker. [...] G Andrew Wilson

Hi Product Hunt, I'm Andrew, the maker.

I run Claude Code and Codex on a MacBook and it kept getting hot, with no way to tell which agent was responsible. Activity Monitor shows dozens of node and compiler processes and no temperature at all.

WhoIsCooking shows the chip temperature in your notch or menu bar, groups each agent session with everything it started into one row, and has a "Cool down my Mac" button that moves busy work to the efficiency cores. Nothing is killed or frozen. On my M5, 4 processes flat out went from about 83°C at full speed to about 48°C cooled. The work just runs a bit slower.

Honest limits: it can't cool GPU work or Apple's own processes, and it needs Apple Silicon (M1 to M5) on macOS 14+. [...] It's $5 one time, signed and notarized, no account. I'd love feedback on what else it should show per agent.

For heavier loads, or if you're about to bag it and go, worth turning the feature off first, or use "only while brewing" so it only stays awake while a trigger condition is actually met. No thermal pressure monitoring built in yet, fair callout though, might add something around this angle.

Tony Hou

Hi Product Hunt! I built Awakado because my Mac kept falling asleep in the middle of long Claude Code runs.

It listens to each agent's own hooks, so it knows when an agent is working, waiting for you, stuck at a usage limit, or done. It keeps the Mac awake only while something is working, then lets it sleep a few minutes after the last one finishes.

The part I like most is in Pro: if Claude Code hits its usage limit at 2 am, Awakado lets the Mac sleep and wakes it two minutes before the limit resets, so the run picks up while you're still asleep.

It's free to download; Pro is $9.99 once for 3 Macs. Made by a small studio in New Zealand. I'd love to hear which agents you'd like it to support next.
